turns.content: In the light-Majorana exchange description of neutrinoless double-beta decay, the inverse half-life is written as T_{1/2}^{-1}=G|M|^2m_{bb}^2/m_e^2. What physics is represented by G, M, and m_{bb}?
Why does the effective light-neutrino mass separate from the nuclear and phase-space factors in this regime? Relate the argument to the relevant momentum scales.

Is the remaining separation between the leptonic phase-space factor G and the nuclear matrix element M formally exact? Distinguish a structural factorization approximation from uncertainty in computing M itself.
Which separation is therefore responsible for the standard formula's inexactness?
How confidently can that structural explanation be stated when the size and implementation dependence of the nonseparable corrections are not specified?
Contrast this source of inexactness with the factorization of the effective light-neutrino mass.
Summarize the structural approximation and the light-Majorana regime in which the formula is being used.
